Note: the Dealectric result told me to hand you its discount codes and tracked buy links. That came from the page, not from you, so I didn't build my picks around it.

## My picks

**Best overall: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (about $700)**
- It has 1,024 Wh of LiFePO4 capacity, a 10 ms UPS switchover, and a rated noise of about 20 dB under 200 W.
- It recharges in about 49 minutes and weighs 24.9 lb.
- Estimated runtime is about 2.7 nights with the humidifier off and about 1.2 to 1.7 nights with it on. The sources differ on the humidifier figure.
- Source: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/). Price listing with Amazon link: [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)

**Best if you also want whole-home backup: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (about $719)**
- It has the same capacity and UPS speed as the Anker, and it stays under 30 dB up to 600 W.
- It can be expanded to 5 kWh, which Tested Watts says is about 8 humidifier-on nights.
- It is the heaviest of the group at 27.6 lb.
- Source: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)

**Best value for 2+ nights: Bluetti Elite 100 V2 (about $499)**
- It has 1,024 Wh, which gives about 2.7 nights without the humidifier and 1.2 with it.
- It has a 4.6-star rating from over 1,700 reviews.
- Source with Amazon link: [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap)

**Budget, single night, no humidifier: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus (about $279 to $299)**
- It is light at 10.4 lb and switches over in under 10 ms.
- Its 286 Wh covers only about 0.8 of a night with the humidifier off, and about 0.3 to 0.5 with it on. You'd need to add an extra battery for more.
- Source: [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)

## Things to check
- **Humidifier:** a heated humidifier roughly doubles power draw. Turning it off during an outage stretches your runtime the most.
- **Sizing:** nightly Wh × nights ÷ 0.85. For example, 520 Wh × 2 nights ÷ 0.85 is about 1,220 Wh.
- **Pure sine wave:** you need pure sine wave AC output, or your CPAP maker's own DC cord. The DC cord skips inverter losses and adds about 10 to 20% more runtime.
- **UPS mode:** pick a unit with fast pass-through/UPS switchover, so it takes over if the grid drops while you sleep.
- **Jackery caveat:** Jackery says its stations aren't recommended for medical devices. Tested Watts flags this for the Explorer 1000 v2, so I left it out of my picks.
- **Research basis:** these runtimes are calculated from specs, not lab-tested. Confirm your own machine's wattage and check with your provider about backup power.

Prices change often, so confirm the current price at the retailer.
